  ATTEND OR WATCH THE MEETING
  Members of the public may attend in-person in the Council Chambers or watch the meeting
  through Zoom, City Website (Live Stream) or Cable TV Channel 10. City Council Chamber doors
  open 30 minutes before the meeting start time.

  PUBLIC COMMENT/SPEAKERS
  Members of the public may express comments to the City Council in person at the meeting or
  may submit written comments before or at the meeting. Submit a Public Speaker card or Written
  Comment card to the City Clerk prior to the public comment portion of that item. Public speakers
  are limited to three minutes unless the presiding officer sets a different limit for meeting
  management purposes. An oral summary of written comments may be given at the discretion of
  the presiding officer.

  Written comments may be emailed to the City Clerk's Office at cityclerk@wlv.org no later than
  4:00 p.m. on the meeting date. Written comments will be provided to City Council prior to the
  meeting and posted at https://www.wlv.org/569/City-Council-Supplemental-Packets

  ZOOM VIEWING ONLY:
  Members of the public watching through Zoom will not have the ability to provide comments on
  agenda items. Zoom is offered strictly as an additional viewing platform. To provide comments,
  see Public Comments/Speakers section.

  https://us02web.zoom.us/j/84070910557
  Webinar ID: 840 7091 0557
  One-tap Mobile:
  +16469313860,,84070910557# OR +13017158592,,84070910557#
  Telephone:
  +1 669 900 9128 OR +1 646 931 3860 OR +1 301 715 8592
 Unless the City Council holds a teleconference meeting under AB 2449 (2022) guidelines, the
meeting will not be cancelled if technical issues occur.

In accordance with the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990, if you require a disability-related
modification or accommodation to attend or participate in this meeting, including auxiliary aids or
services, please call the City Clerk’s office at (818) 706-1613 at least 48 hours prior to the meeting.

Any disclosable public records related to an open session item on a regular meeting agenda and
distributed by the City to the City Council less than 72 hours prior to that meeting are available for
public inspection at City Hall (31200 Oak Crest Drive, Westlake Village) during normal business
hours and are posted on the City’s Website - https://www.wlv.org/569/City-Council-Supplemental-
Packets.

  CALL TO ORDER:

  This regular meeting of the Westlake Village City Council was called to order by Mayor
  Mcsweeney on Wednesday, March 25, 2026 at 6:31 p.m., at 31200 Oak Crest Drive,
  Westlake Village.

  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE:

  Mayor Mcsweeney invited Kate Vong and Candence Lee to lead the Pledge of
  Allegiance.

  ROLL CALL:

  PRESENT:  Councilmernbers Honig, Davis, Pearl, Mayor Pro Tern Halpern, and
  Mayor Mcsweeney

  ABSENT:  None

  Also Present:  City Manager de Geus, City Attorney Boga, Assistant City Manager
  Wilson, City Clerk Mann, Planning Director Asp, City Engineer
  Hughes, Assistant to the City Manager Mott, Associate Planner Orr,
  and Planning Intern Anya Kargodorian.

  APPROVAL OF MINUTES:

  Mayor Pro Tern Halpern moved to approve the Minutes of March 11, 2026 City Council
  Closed Session and Regular Meeting. Councilrnernber Pearl seconded the motion.

  NO:

   City Council Minutes
City of Westlake Village  March 25, 2026  2

APPROVAL OF AGENDA:

Councilmember Pearl moved to approve the Agenda as presented. Mayor Pro Tern
Halpern seconded the motion.

  YES:  Councilmembers Honig, Davis, Pearl, Mayor Pro Tern Halpern, and
  Mayor Mcsweeney
  NO:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

Mayor Mcsweeney declared the motion passed 5-0.

SPECIAL PRESENTATIONS/CEREMONIAL MATTERS:

Kate Vong, Westlake High School, and Candence Lee, Newbury Park High School,
apprised City Council about their initiative call "Team Roll Over Cancer for Blood Cancer
United Student Visionaries Program" and highlighted their fundraising efforts. They have
led a community wide fundraising and awareness campaign. City Council congratulated
them on their efforts and encouraged them to continue in their awareness efforts.

Danielle Borja, President and Chief Executive Officer for the Conejo Valley Chamber of
Commerce, advised Mayor Mcsweeney that she has been selected as the 2026
Chamber's Woman of the Year. Ms. Borja read from the nomination submittal, highlighted
Mayor McSweeney's accomplishments and invited Mayor Mcsweeney to the upcoming
Gala, May 15, 2026, to receive her award.

Ms. Borja and Chamber Ambassadors presented balloons to Mayor Mcsweeney. City
Council stated how proud they are of Mayor Mcsweeney, presented flowers to Mayor
Mcsweeny and stated that they are looking forward to celebrating with her on May 15,
2026.

PUBLIC COMMENTS: None

COUNCIL RESPONSE:

STAFF COMMENTS:

City Manager de Geus congratulated Mayor Mcsweeney on the 2026 Woman of the Year
Award. Mr. de Geus provided updates on recent community beautification projects
(Community Park Entry Signage and Sight Line Improvement, new trash cans, sidewalk
repairs and Berniece Bennet Park Playground project).

Mr. de Geus announced Earth Day and a final reminder for nominations for Citizen and
Youth of the Year (closing March 31, 2026) and Westlake Village Community-Foundation
Scholarship applications (due by March 31, 2026).
   City Council Minutes
  City of Westlake Village  March 25, 2026  3

  STAFF COMMENTS (continued):

l  Mr. de Gues announced that Associate Planner Miles Orr is leaving the City and wished
  him good luck on his next position at the City of Los Angeles.

  City Manager de Geus previewed upcoming Council Committee and City Council agenda
  items.

  COUNCIL COMMENTS:

  Councilmember Honig inquired on the number of Leaf Blower rebates received to date.
  Staff advised that 67 applications have been processed.

  Councilmember Davis advised residents that some snakes are good and to not be afraid
  of all snakes.

  MONTHLY DEPARTMENTAL REPORTS:

  1.  Sheriff's Department Report

  Captain Dustin Carr presented the Sheriff Department's report for the month of
  February 2026 covering crime statistics.  Captain Carr highlighted a recent E-
  Bikes operation, Feeding the Military Event, and Station position vacancies. He
  also announced the Annual Station Open House will be held on May 2, 2026 from
  9 am - Noon.

  Captain Carr addressed City Council questions about Flock Cameras and how the
  Cameras have assisted with solving crimes. Related to E-Bikes, Councilmember
  Davis suggested an bike event at White Oak Elementary to educate the young
  students on E-bike safety.

  2.  Fire Department Report

  Assistant Fire Chief Drew Smith presented the Fire Department's report for the
  month of February 2026 including the number of fires, medical response calls, and
  rescue activities conducted.

j
  3.  Library Report

  Julie Frieze, Manager, Westlake Village Daniel K. Ludwig Library, presented the
  library's report for the month of February 2026 covering traffic, circulation,
  programs, and reference requests.
   City Council Minutes
City of Westlake Village  March 25, 2026  4

CITY COUNCIL COMMITTEE REPORTS:

  1. 2035 STRATEGIC PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE REPORT - UPDATE ON
  THE 2035 STRATEGIC PLAN PROCESS

  City Manager de Geus presented an update on the development of the 2035
  Strategic Plan. He reported that the Strategic Plan Advisory Committee has met
  seven times since May 2025 to review the existing 2025 Strategic Plan, assess
  community feedback, and develop updated draft values, mission, and vision
  statements. Mr. de Geus noted that the Committee also considered results from
  the October 2025 Community Survey, which showed strong resident satisfaction
  with Westlake Village and a consistent desire to preserve the community's
  character. Committee members reviewed stakeholder input, partner agency
  perspectives,  and  Strengths/Weaknesses/Opportunities/Threats  (SWOT)
  analyses and have drafted six proposed goals along with preliminary objectives
  and strategies.

  City Manager de Geus stated that the Committee reached consensus on the draft
  foundational statements at its March 2026 meeting and continues to refine
  goal-related programs. The first full draft of the 2035 Strategic Plan will be
  presented at the joint Study Session with the City Council on April 22, 2026. Staff
  requested that the Council review the draft goals and objectives and provide any
  feedback to guide finalization of the plan.

  City Council received the update and commented on how the draft is quite easy to
  read and follow.

PUBLIC HEARING:

  1. CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT NO. 21-001: RESOLUTION NO. 2446-26

  Planning Intern Kargodorian presented a request for approval of a time extension
  of Conditional Use Permit No. 21-001 to allow continued operation of the existing
  Pilates studio at 31149 Via Colinas, Suite 605. The studio's use remains
  consistent with the La Baya Zoning District of the North Business Park Specific
  Plan and continues to operate within the previously approved class sizes, hours,
  and floor plan. The use was found to be compatible with surrounding commercial
  tenants and adequately served by existing parking.

  On March 4, 2026, the Land Use Committee (Halpern/Pearl) was unable to review
  due to a lack of quorum. As applicants were already waiting at City Hall,
  Councilmember Pearl was briefed on this item and recommended that the request
  proceed to the City Council for a Public Hearing.

  Michelle Zimmer, on behalf of Pilates Addiction, addressed City Council.
   City Council Minutes
  City of Westlake Village  March 25, 2026  5

  PUBLIC HEARING (continued):

l
  Mayor Pro Tern Halpern moved that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 2446-
  26, determining Conditional Use Permit No. 21-001, Modification No. 1 is exempt
  from CEQA and authorize the continued operation of a Pilates studio located at
  31149 Via Colinas, Suite No. 605 (Pilates Addiction). Councilmember Davis
  seconded the motion.

  YES:  Councilmembers Honig, Davis, Pearl, Mayor Pro Tern
  Halpern, and Mayor Mcsweeney
  NO:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

  Mayor Mcsweeney declared the motion passed 5-0.

  RESOLUTION NO. 2446-26: A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY
  OF WESTLAKE VILLAGE APPROVING CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT NO. 21-001,
  MODIFICATION NO. 1 TO AUTHORIZE THE CONTINUED OPERATION OF A PILATES
  STUDIO LOCATED AT 31149 VIA COLINAS, SUITE NO. 605 (PILATES ADDICTION)

  MONTHLY IN-HOUSE DEPARTMENTAL REPORTS:

  1.  Engineering Department Report

  City Engineer Hughes provided the Engineering Report highlighting the Civic
  Center projects and the Pure Water Project. The status of the various projects at
  the Civic Center were discussed.

  2.  Planning Department Report

  Planning Director Asp provided the Planning Department Report highlighting the
  upcoming Shred Event on April 18, 2026 from 9 am - noon, Accessory Dwelling
  Unit Ordinance modification, and announced the General Plan Hazard Update
  project with a meeting held on March 16, 2026.

j  3.  Cultural Recreation Report

  Assistant to the City Manager Mott provided an update on upcoming Cultural and
  Recreation events. The City-to-Schools program will conclude with a field trip to
  City Hall on April 15, 2026 and attendance at the April 22, 2026 City Council
  meeting. The annual Earth Day activities include a trail clean-up on April 11, 2026
  at the Wishbone Trail, the Bi-Annual Shred Event at City Hall on April 18, 2026,
  and the Earth Day Festival on April 25, 2026 featuring partner booths and
  community activities.
   City Council Minutes
City of Westlake Village  March 25, 2026  6

CONSENT CALENDAR:

Councilmember Pearl moved to approve the Consent Calendar. Councilmember Davis
seconded the motion.

  YES:  Councilmembers Honig, Davis, Pearl, Mayor Pro Tern
  Halpern, and Mayor Mcsweeney
  NO:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

Mayor Mcsweeney declared the motion passed 5-0.

  APPROVAL OF WARRANTS: Warrants effective March 15, 2026 in the amount
  of $957,646.69

  GENERAL BUSINESS:

  1.  ADOPTION OF ORDINANCE NO 313-26. ORDINANCE TITLE: AN
  ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF WESTLAKE VILLAGE APPROVING AN
  AMENDMENT TO ITS CONTRACT WITH THE BOARD OF
  ADMINISTRATION OF THE CALIFORNIA PUBLIC EMPLOYEES'
  RETIREMENT SYSTEM - City Council waived the second reading and
  adopted Ordinance No. 313-26.

  ORDINANCE NO. 313-26: AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE
  CITY OF WESTLAKE VILLAGE APPROVING AN AMENDMENT TO ITS
  CONTRACT WITH THE BOARD OF ADMINISTRATION OF THE CALIFORNIA
  PUBLIC EMPLOYEES' RETIREMENT SYSTEM

  2.  RIGHT OF ENTRY AGREEMENT WITH WESTLAKE VILLAGE GOLF
  COURSE FOR THE 2026 FIREWORKS EVENT - City Council approved
  the Right of Entry Agreement with the Westlake Village Golf Course for the
  2026 July 4th fireworks event and authorized the Mayor to sign and execute
  the agreement on behalf of the City.

OLD BUSINESS:

  1. THOUSAND OAKS BOULEVARD MEDIAN TURNKEY TRANSFORMATION
  GRANT PROJECT UPDATE: SAFETY STRIP

  Assistant to the City Manager Mott provided an update on the Thousand Oaks
  Boulevard Median Turnkey Transformation Project, funded through the California
  Department of Water Resources (DWR) and the Inland Empire Utilities Agency
  (IEUA). The award provided approximately $504,771 in construction funding for
  the Westlake Village portion of the project. Median concept designs were approved
   City Council Minutes
  City of Westlake Village  March 25, 2026  7

  OLD BUSINESS (continued):

l  by the City Council on February 11, 2026, and the final scope of work was
  completed on March 13, 2026 following coordination among City departments, Las
  Virgenes Municipal Water District (LVMWD), and Brightview Landscape Services.
  Turf removal is scheduled for early April, and construction is expected to take 30
  to 40 working days.

  Staff presented two safety strip material options, Granite 3"-6" and Can Mix, and
  requested Council direction to finalize the design. Mr. Mott noted that the City's
  allocated $200,000 budget covers non-grant portions of the project, with final bids
  pending. Nearby businesses have been notified, and public communication will
  continue as construction begins.

  City Council discussion included the cost for the safety strip and the materials
  selected.

  City Council direct staff to pause the implementation of the Safety Strip in the
  Thousand Oaks Boulevard Median Turnkey Transformation project and explore
  this addition at a later date.

  NEW BUSINESS:

  1. ACCEPTANCE OF A FULFILLMENT AGREEMENT.(92000000000FUL08) WITH
  LOS ANGELES COUNTY METROPOLITAN TRANSPORTATION AUTHORITY
  FOR THE FISCAL YEAR 2025-26 ANNUAL STREET IMPROVEMENT
  PROJECT  •

  City Engineer Hughes presented a request for approval of a fulfillment agreement
  with Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority (LACMTA) to
  convert the City's remaining Surface Transportation Program-Local (STP-L)
  balance into $70,945 of Proposition C funds. These funds will reimburse part of
  the fiscal year (FY) 2025-26 Annual Street Improvement Project, which includes
  pavement maintenance in the Lakeshore and Southridge Trails neighborhoods
  and along Via Rocas. Ms. Hughes noted that the project is already fully funded in

j  the City's budget, and accepting the agreement will allow the City to seek
  reimbursement for eligible construction costs.

  Councilmember Pearl moved that the City Council approve fulfillment agreement
  FA 920000000000FUL08 in the amount of $70,945 with Los Angeles County
  Metropolitan Transportation Authority for the FY 2025-26 Annual Street
  Improvement Project; and authorize the Mayor to sign and execute the agreement
  on behalf of the City. Councilmember Davis seconded the motion.
   City Council Minutes
City of Westlake Village  March 25, 2026  8

NEW BUSINESS (continued):

  YES:  Councilmembers Honig, Davis, Pearl, Mayor Pro Tern
  Halpern, and Mayor Mcsweeney
  NO:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

Mayor Mcsweeney declared the motion passed 5-0.

ADJOURNMENT:

Mayor Mcsweeney adjourned the meeting at 8:39 p.m.
